facts.text: Basalt earned its name from the basalt rock deposits that surround the original town site.
Pioneers settled Basalt in the mid‑1880s, attracted by fertile Snake River plains that promised homesteading and irrigation farming.
Early roads linked Basalt homesteads to the railroad, while settlers dug a communal irrigation canal and built a log schoolhouse.
Outcrops of the Columbia River Basalt Group dot the area, underscoring Basalt’s volcanic roots and shaping its identity.
Basalt experiences hot 85°F summer days and cold 16°F winter nights, a wide diurnal swing driven by high elevation and clear skies.
Soils here stem from volcanic basalt, making them shallow, stony, alkaline, which limits water retention and steers local plant life.
